lines.rookie: You came on the noon train. You were never on the platform.
lines.junior: You arrived on the noon train. You were never on the platform.
lines.master: You came in on the noon train; you were never on the platform.

lines.rookie: That is true. I wrote what the traveller said.
lines.junior: That's true. I wrote down what the traveller told me.
lines.master: True enough. I wrote what the traveller said.

lines.rookie: That does not show where my story came from.
lines.junior: That doesn't show where my story came from.
lines.master: That proves nothing about where my story came from.

lines.rookie: Mr. Pak's day shows when the writer came.
lines.junior: Mr. Pak's day shows when the writer arrived.
lines.master: Mr. Pak's day reveals when the writer arrived.

lines.rookie: Mr. Sorin asks: "Then what did he call out?"
lines.junior: Mr. Sorin asks: "Then what did he call out?"
lines.master: Mr. Sorin asks: "Then what did he call out?"

lines.rookie: "Korea, hurrah!" Mr. Pak heard it on the platform.
lines.junior: "Korea, hurrah!" Mr. Pak heard those words on the platform.
lines.master: "Korea, hurrah!" Mr. Pak heard it himself, on the platform.

lines.rookie: Not a word about money, then.
lines.junior: So there was not a word about money.
lines.master: Not a word of money, then.

lines.rookie: That does not say what he called out.
lines.junior: That doesn't say what he called out.
lines.master: That tells me nothing of what he called out.

lines.rookie: Mr. Pak's words say what was called out.
lines.junior: Mr. Pak's words tell you what was called out.
lines.master: Mr. Pak's words record what was called out.

lines.rookie: Mr. Sorin asks: "Why would a man call out for Korea?"
lines.junior: Mr. Sorin asks: "Why would a man call out for Korea?"
lines.master: Mr. Sorin asks: "Why would a man call out for Korea?"

lines.rookie: In 1905, Japan forced a treaty on Korea.
lines.junior: In 1905, Japan forced a treaty on Korea.
lines.master: In 1905, Japan forced a treaty upon Korea.

lines.rookie: The Emperor's envoys went to The Hague. They were not let in.
lines.junior: The Emperor's envoys went to The Hague, but they were not let in.
lines.master: The Emperor's envoys travelled to The Hague, only to be turned away.

lines.rookie: So he called out for Korea. Not for money.
lines.junior: So he called out for Korea, not for money.
lines.master: So he called out for Korea, and not for money.

lines.rookie: That does not tell me what Korea lost.
lines.junior: That doesn't tell me what Korea lost.
lines.master: That says nothing of what Korea lost.

lines.rookie: The Emperor's letter shows what happened to Korea in 1905.
lines.junior: The Emperor's letter shows what happened to Korea in 1905.
lines.master: The Emperor's letter reveals what befell Korea in 1905.

lines.rookie: CLOSE THE CASE
lines.junior: CLOSE THE CASE
lines.master: CLOSE THE CASE

lines.rookie: Tomorrow I will print what Mr. Pak heard.
lines.junior: Tomorrow I will print what Mr. Pak heard.
lines.master: Tomorrow my paper will carry what Mr. Pak heard.

lines.rookie: He called out, "Korea, hurrah!" Not for money.
lines.junior: He called out, "Korea, hurrah!" It was not for money.
lines.master: He called out, "Korea, hurrah!" Money had nothing to do with it.

lines.rookie: In prison, An Jung-geun began writing 'On Peace in East Asia'.
lines.junior: In prison, An Jung-geun started writing 'On Peace in East Asia'.
lines.master: In prison, An Jung-geun set about writing 'On Peace in East Asia'.

lines.rookie: He wrote about Korea's independence and peace in East Asia.
lines.junior: In it, he wrote about Korea's independence and peace in East Asia.
lines.master: In it he wrote of Korea's independence and of peace in East Asia.

lines.rookie: He began it in March 1910, and could not finish it.
lines.junior: He started it in March 1910, but he could not finish it.
lines.master: He began it in March 1910, yet was never able to finish it.

lines.rookie: One day, all of Korea will call out too.
lines.junior: One day, the whole of Korea will call out too.
lines.master: One day, all of Korea will call out as well.
